title: Prefix domination for geometric weights
statement: Let $N\ge 0$, let $0\le\rho\le1$, and let $a,b:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$. Suppose that for every integer $j$ with $0\le j\le N$, $\sum_{k=0}^{j-1}b(k)\le\sum_{k=0}^{j-1}a(k)$, and that $\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}b(k)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a(k)$, with an empty sum interpreted as zero. Then $\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\rho^k b(k)\le\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\rho^k a(k)$.
hypotheses_covered: $\rho$ lies between zero and one, inclusive
Every prefix sum of $b$ through length at most $N$ is at most the corresponding prefix sum of $a$
The sums of $a$ and $b$ over the first $N$ terms are equal
replaced:
Let $N\in\mathbb N$, $\rho\in[0,1]$, and $a,b:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ satisfy
$\sum_{k=0}^{j-1}b(k)\le\sum_{k=0}^{j-1}a(k)$ for every integer $0\le j\le N$ and
$\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}b(k)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a(k)$, with sums over no indices interpreted as zero.
Then
\[
 \sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\rho^k b(k)\le\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\rho^k a(k).
\]
